https://www.travelerstoday.com/articles/.text: Celine Dion opens her first full concert residency in more than six years on Saturday, September 12, at Paris's Plenitude Arena — and the demand her comeback has created is reshaping both travel prices and the risks fans face before they ever reach the door. International flight searches to Paris for the September 12 through October 17 residency window are up 11% year-over-year, and confirmed bookings have risen 5%, according to Amadeus Travel Intelligence data pulled in mid-August.But the bigger problem for fans traveling from the US, Brazil, Canada, and elsewhere is not the cost of the flight — it is the near-certainty that some of them are holding fake tickets. The arena's lawyers have identified nearly 200 fraudulent websites and social media accounts impersonating Dion, Plenitude Arena, Ticketmaster, and AXS, targeting international fans who missed the initial sale when 9 million lottery entrants competed for tickets that sold out within hours. Cybersecurity firm Group-IB, which documented the coordinated fraud campaign, says scammers are operating through multiple channels. Arena officials say they are bracing for hundreds of scam victims per night.Where Are the Most Paris-Bound Fans Coming From?The Americas are driving the sharpest flight demand increase. According to Amadeus Travel Intelligence, the United States accounts for 26.5% of international search traffic and 26.85% of confirmed bookings for the residency period — more than any other country. Brazil represents 11% of searches and 5.5% of bookings, while Canada, Dion's home country, contributes 7.4% of searches and 4.4% of bookings. Together, those three countries account for nearly 45% of the global surge in Paris flight searches.Mexico and Brazil are two of the fastest-growing booking markets, with year-over-year growth of 38% and 30% respectively for the residency period.Asia-Pacific markets are the fastest-growing overall. Thailand has seen a 200% increase in bookings compared to the same period last year, Japan is up 40%, and India up 13%. Japan (6.6%), Australia (5.1%), South Korea (4.5%), and India (2.19%) together represent 18.4% of all international travelers booked to Paris during Dion's dates, according to Amadeus.European markets present a different picture. Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Portugal, and Poland together represent 26.5% of international flight searches during the residency period — but European travelers convert to bookings at a much lower rate, accounting for just over 5% of confirmed international reservations. Greece leads European search growth at 116% year-over-year, but Greek travelers are largely browsing rather than booking.How Much Are Paris Hotels Costing Right Now?Paris hotel revenue per available room during the residency period has reached $211, a 13% increase over the same stretch last year, according to Amadeus Demand360 hotel data.The residency is also lengthening trips. While short stays of one to five nights still account for 47.45% of hotel bookings for the period, bookings for stays of six to thirteen nights — the category Amadeus tracks as "medium-length" — are running 6% higher than in 2025, representing 41.42% of all hotel reservations. Amadeus describes this as consistent with the "culture tripping" pattern in which fans build a concert into a broader holiday rather than making a quick in-and-out trip.Natixis CIB, a French investment bank, projected the 16 fall dates alone would attract roughly 480,000 spectators to the French capital. Total economic impact — spanning tickets, accommodation, transport, and dining — is estimated at up to €1 billion for the Île-de-France region, with Natixis CIB putting the range at €570 million to €1 billion. Those figures are projections, not realized totals.Are Celine Dion Tickets Still Available for Paris?The standard seats for all 16 fall dates sold out within hours of going on sale. A limited number of VIP packages priced from approximately €1,099 are still available through the official Plenitude Arena website, and official fan-to-fan resale is now open on the authorized platforms — at the original ticket price — for fans who can no longer attend.A broader secondary market exists, but it carries severe risk. Plenitude Arena's marketing director, Céline Trioux, identified only three platforms as authorized for resale: AXS France, Ticketmaster France, and Fnac Spectacles. Any ticket offered through social media — Facebook groups, Instagram posts, TikTok offers, or X — cannot be authenticated. Screenshots of barcodes are especially unreliable because Plenitude Arena uses dynamic, rotating QR codes that invalidate static images.The 2027 leg of the residency — 10 additional shows scheduled for May 2027, bringing the total run to 26 concerts — may still have limited availability through the official authorized sellers.What Should Fans Know About the Celine Dion Ticket Scam?Group-IB's findings show scammers are operating through two main channels. The first is Facebook fan communities, where sellers build credibility through private messages and voice recordings before deploying pressure tactics — "multiple other buyers are interested, the ticket sells in minutes" — to push a fast decision. The second is a network of fake websites cloning Ticketmaster, AXS, and the venue.A newer risk involves deepfake video. Brian Long, CEO of cybersecurity firm Adaptive Security, said fans should treat any video of a celebrity appearing to offer discounted tickets or presale access as a fraud signal, regardless of how convincing it appears. "A video of Dion, or any major artist, appearing to offer discounted tickets or exclusive presale access should immediately raise flags," Long said.Plenitude Arena expects to turn away hundreds of fans with fake tickets across the residency. Based on its experience with Taylor Swift's Eras Tour shows at the same venue — where approximately 400 to 500 fans were turned away with counterfeit tickets — the arena has set up a dedicated complaints desk at the entrance where staff will receive scam victims and explain the process for filing a police complaint.Victims generally have no fast recourse. A ticket discovered as fraudulent at the door is gone; money paid to an unauthorized reseller through Facebook or a cloned website is almost certainly unrecoverable without formal French police and banking action.Why Is Dion's Paris Return Such a Milestone?Dion publicly disclosed her diagnosis of stiff-person syndrome — a rare, progressive neurological and autoimmune disorder causing severe muscle rigidity and painful spasms — in December 2022, having already been forced to cancel her Courage World Tour dates.Her first public performance after the diagnosis came at the opening ceremony of the Paris 2024 Summer Olympics, where she performed from the Eiffel Tower in the rain, singing "Hymne à l'amour," — a moment that drew global attention and signaled she was continuing to fight for a return to the stage.The Paris residency at Plenitude Arena — Europe's largest indoor arena, with a capacity of up to 45,000 — was announced on March 30, 2026, Dion's 58th birthday, via an emotional video broadcast beneath the Eiffel Tower. More than 9 million fans entered a lottery for priority access, and all 16 dates sold out within hours. The shows run on Wednesdays, Fridays, and Saturdays from September 12 through October 17 at 8 p.m. local Paris time. The fall program is scheduled to include both French and English material.

https://www.dw.com/en/anthropic-report-i.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5NTaF The Claude app was allegedly misused by Russian agents Image: Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto/picture alliance Advertisement In Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic , Russian agents are said to have deliberately used the AI assistant Claude to promote pro-Russian influence. A report titled " Detecting and Countering Misuse of AI ," published by US-based company Anthropic in September, detailed how opposition politicians were monitored, propaganda content was created and disinformation campaigns were supported. The report claimed that Claude was used primarily to produce content broadcast by Radio Lengo Songo, a radio station that, according to the international investigative collective All Eyes on Wagner, is funded by Russia. The collective, made up of journalists, academics and experts, investigates the activities of the Russian mercenary Wagner Group and its successor structures, such as the Africa Corps, around the world. Pro-Russian propaganda, surveillance of the opposition The Anthropic report said the content was pro-Russian and portrayed the Central African government and the Africa Corps mercenaries in a positive light, while taking a critical stance on France and the opposition. According to Anthropic, Russia is using AI in African countries to spread its messages Image: Fred de Noyelle/Godong/picture alliance Lou Osborn, a member of All Eyes on Wagner, was involved in the research for the latest report. He believes these methods are part of a practice that has already been observed in connection with the Wagner Group in the Central African Republic. "There have been several arrests of people who were not necessarily closely affiliated with the Touadera regime," he told DW. "They’ve been doing this for several years now." Faustin-Archange Touadera has been president of the Central African Republic since 2016. "The arrests were the subject of online campaigns in newspapers and on the radio which portrayed those individuals either as proxies for France or Western intelligence services, or as people preparing a coup against Touadera," Osborn added. Anthropic also reported that Claude was prompted to portray opposition figures as armed militants in an effort to provoke security forces into taking action against them. Anthropic says Claude refused the request. However, the report did not name the opposition figures who were monitored, specify the exact nature of the data collected, or say who received it. 'The government wants to get rid of us,' opposition says For the opposition, the Anthropic report underscored the determination of the government in Bangui and its Russian allies to get rid of them. Martin Ziguele, chairman of the Movement for the Liberation of the Central African People, referred to an earlier case. "We have been observing this since 2020, when the CPC, a coalition of rebel groups, attacked Bangui. Strangely enough, several media outlets did everything in their power to establish alleged links between certain opposition leaders and the CPC," Ziguele told DW. "There were also attacks against the opposition claiming that we were being paid by foreign countries. There was an attempt to pass a law stating that foreign agents were present in the country. All of this relates to the activities of the Wagner Group, as does this latest revelation." An arial view of Bangui, Central African Republic Image: Sam Mednick/AP Photo/picture alliance DW also sought a statement from Russia. "Yes, I heard about [the report] in the news," said Dmitri Sytyi, a representative of the Russian mission in the Central African Republic. "But there are no concrete facts in it. [...] These are vague allegations, without precision and without evidence." AI influence operations across the DRC, Kenya, Sudan and Mali? Russia firmly denies the allegations, but the report indicates that the Central African Republic was not an isolated case. According to the report, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Kenya , Sudan and Mali were also affected. In the DRC, Anthropic identified 318 articles that, according to the report, were published by a network of about 70 fake news sites and subsequently distributed by more than 250 fictitious accounts on X. The content supported the positions of the Congolese government against the backdrop of the conflict with Rwanda. In Kenya, Claude was allegedly used to generate batches of 50 messages at a time that supported the government and were hostile toward the opposition. Anthropic co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei Image: Don Feria/AP Photo/picture alliance In Sudan, Anthropic says AI was used as part of an operation attributed to individuals in the United Arab Emirates — particularly to create fabricated witness statements for the United Nations. In Mali, meanwhile, an adviser with ties to intelligence services allegedly used Claude to develop a platform for monitoring telecommunications. According to the report, it was designed to target 25 million SIM cards and circumvent the requirement to obtain judicial authorization. Anthropic says it uncovered and shut down all of these different operations between December 2025 and August 2026, primarily by deleting the accounts involved and strengthening its detection systems. This article was originally published in German.
